intro: You have reached Palu, an ancient city in Elazığ province, lived in from the 9th century BC to today. This historic town lies east of the Euphrates, and above it stands a castle bearing Urartian inscriptions.
history: Palu once guarded the western frontier of Urartu. Empires changed, but its role did not: under Rome and Byzantium it remained a fortified town. And the Urartian inscription at the castle gate? You can still read it today.
structure-1: You are now at Palu Castle, the historic fortress east of the Euphrates. Look for the Urartian inscription it bears.
structure-3: Here is the Cimşit Bey Bath, an Ottoman-era bathhouse at Palu. Imagine the warmth and the voices once filling its rooms.
structure-5: Now to the Old Bridge. These are the remains of the historic bridge over the Murat, a branch of the Euphrates.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Urartian Inscription and the Great Mosque.
facts: Did you know? Palu Castle holds a cuneiform rock inscription in the citadel thought to belong to the Urartian king Menua, and it is among the westernmost proofs of Urartian reach. Old Palu was abandoned after earthquakes in the twentieth century, and today it stands as a ghost settlement of mosque, church and houses.
outro: This brings our tour of Palu to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
